title: Mittag-Leffler characterization by eventual domination
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $M$ be an $R$-module, and let $(M_i,f_{ij})$ be a directed system of finitely presented $R$-modules with colimit $M$ and canonical maps $f_i:M_i\to M$. For maps $a:P\to Q$ and $b:P\to Q'$ of $R$-modules, say that $b$ dominates $a$ if for every $R$-module $L$ one has $\ker(a\otimes_R\mathrm{id}_L)\subseteq\ker(b\otimes_R\mathrm{id}_L)$. Then $M$ is Mittag-Leffler in the tensor-product sense [def-trf-mittag-leffler-module] if and only if for every $i$ there exists $j\ge i$ such that $f_{ij}:M_i\to M_j$ dominates $f_i:M_i\to M$.

source.place: Tag 059E, proposition-ML-characterization, equivalence of conditions (2) and the tensor-product Mittag-Leffler condition

proof.text: Assume $M$ is tensor Mittag-Leffler and fix $i\in I$. Choose the single target $P=\prod_{s\in I}M_s$ before choosing any later stage. For every source index $r$, [lem-trf-mittag-leffler-hom-systems] applied with $N=P$ supplies $s\ge r$ stabilizing the precomposition images into $P$ for all $t\ge s$. These are exactly the quantified hypotheses of [lem-trf-hom-product-stabilization-factorization] for the same small nonempty directed system. Its conclusion at our fixed $i$ supplies $j\ge i$ and maps $h_k:M_k\to M_j$ with $h_k\circ f_{ik}=f_{ij}$ for every $k\ge i$. Restrict to $k\ge j$; neither $j$ nor this family depends on a tensor-test module.

source.place: Tags 059M and 059E, Hom stabilization into the product and eventual transition factorizations

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-tail-factorizations-tensor-kernel] with the given colimit, the fixed $i\le j$, and the maps $h_k$ for all $k\ge j$ from Step 1. The same $j$ works for every $R$-module $L$, giving $\ker(f_i\otimes\mathrm{id}_L)\subseteq\ker(f_{ij}\otimes\mathrm{id}_L)$. This is precisely domination of $f_i$ by $f_{ij}$. Since $i$ was arbitrary, the forward implication follows.

Conversely assume eventual domination. Fix a set $A$, modules $(L_\alpha)$, put $V=\prod_\alpha L_\alpha$, and take $x\in\ker\theta_{M,(L_\alpha)}$. The small nonempty directed index is filtered. By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-commutes-with-colimits], the maps $f_i\otimes\mathrm{id}_V$ exhibit $M\otimes_RV$ as the colimit of $M_i\otimes_RV$, with transition maps $f_{ik}\otimes\mathrm{id}_V$. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise] gives $i,z$ with $x=(f_i\otimes\mathrm{id}_V)(z)$. For this $i$, choose $j\ge i$ from eventual domination: its kernel inclusion holds for every test module $L$, simultaneously for $V$ and all $L_\alpha$. Only one such $j$ is needed for this lifted element; no family of choices over all source indices is required.

source.place: Tag 059M, proposition-ML-tensor, (1) implies (2), lifting a comparison-kernel element to a stage; Tags 00DD and 00D7

proof.text: Use [lem-trf-fp-factorization-product-kernel] with $P=M_i$, $Q=M_j$, $T=M$, $a=f_{ij}$, $b=f_i$, $c=f_j$, and the family and lifted element $z$ from Step 3. The module $Q=M_j$ is finitely presented and $b=c\circ a$ is the cocone identity. Our chosen $j$ gives precisely $\ker(b\otimes\mathrm{id}_L)\subseteq\ker(a\otimes\mathrm{id}_L)$ for every $L$; moreover $\theta_{T,(L_\alpha)}((b\otimes\mathrm{id}_V)z)=\theta_{M,(L_\alpha)}(x)=0$. The helper therefore gives $(a\otimes\mathrm{id}_V)z=0$ and $(b\otimes\mathrm{id}_V)z=0$, the latter being $x=0$. For equal comparison images of $u,v$, apply this to $u-v$ to obtain $u=v$. Thus every comparison is injective, the condition of [def-trf-mittag-leffler-module].

source.place: Tag 059M, proposition-ML-tensor, product-comparison diagram and injectivity conclusion
